warning_source: Bini Kfir / Moshav Tkuma standby-squad commander
recipient: Senior Gaza-area IDF officer / previous brigade commander; regional-council heads
warning_summary: Kfir says he repeatedly warned that removing rifles from the local standby squad left roughly 800 residents without an operable first-response force against infiltration, and that a senior/brigade commander dismissed the concern by relying on the Gaza barrier.
evidence_update: Ynet (6 Nov 2023) records Kfir saying he warned a senior officer and wrote regional-council heads that there effectively was no standby squad without weapons. Makor Rishon independently published a later interview with the same witness quoting the brigade commander as saying there was no threat because Gaza was contained behind the barriers. The underlying weapon-removal/readiness gap is corroborated by later reporting and IDF/community investigations, but the delivery evidence still comes from Kfir himself.
gaps: Post-event first-person warning claim has not yet been independently corroborated by a contemporaneous letter, named recipient, council record, or second witness. Recover the written message to council heads and identify/date the brigade-commander meeting before acceptance. Do not infer that weapon policy caused any specific Oct. 7 outcome.

recipient: Defense Ministry; IDF; Finance Ministry; historical responsible bodies
warning_summary: The May 2026 audit formally confirms that local military-security coordinators and standby squads are a core component of community defense against killing-spree infiltrations and documents longstanding command/interface and communications-equipment deficiencies.
evidence_update: Official State Comptroller report published 12 May 2026 says some problems in the operation/employment of security coordinators had first been flagged by the Comptroller roughly 20 years earlier and remained unresolved; it also records communications-equipment gaps and unclear interfaces between local security officials and the IDF. This strengthens the documentary basis for the older/local-readiness evidence chain.
gaps: The 2026 report does not by itself establish a distinct pre-Oct. 7 warning delivered to named members of the 2023 government. Use as corroborating/historical context unless the underlying earlier audit(s), recipients and delivery chain are recovered.

warning_source: Giora Zaltz / Upper Galilee Regional Council head
recipient: Benjamin Netanyahu; IDF chief; Northern Command chief (publicly addressed)
warning_summary: Zaltz warned that excluding northern local authorities from security planning and preparedness was a mistake for which residents could pay a heavy price amid Hezbollah escalation.
evidence_update: Lane 5 rechecked the northern-border July sequence and direct local-leader/IDF contacts. The warning remains substantively relevant and contemporaneous, but no direct delivery/receipt record for the July 30 statement was recovered.
gaps: Need letter/message/minutes or acknowledged receipt by PMO, IDF chief or Northern Command. Public appeal alone does not establish delivery.

warning_summary: During direct calls after multi-front rocket fire, local leaders raised urgent protection/shelter requests; Netanyahu instructed the PMO director to address urgent protection requests.
evidence_update: Contemporaneous N12 and Walla reporting establishes direct contact and PMO follow-up. The event is useful corroboration for already accepted local-protection/readiness warnings, especially northern shelter gaps and Gaza-envelope preparedness, but does not add sufficiently distinct warning content to justify another database unit.
gaps: Keep as corroboration rather than duplicate unless a separate contemporaneous warning document with distinct threat content surfaces.
